reason: B offers the stronger controlled test by using near-isovalent substitutions to vary atomic-size mismatch while approximately holding electron count constant, then measuring local distortion, Tc, and Hc2 against the starting alloy. Its evidence does not directly establish distortion as the controlling mechanism and the titanium-rich setting remains close to an already studied class, but A is less discriminating and relies on the physically unsupported generalization that increasing heavy-transition-metal content should enhance electron–phonon coupling.
